newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral sets up panel to boost exports.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral sets up panel to boost exports.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Thursday announced the setting up of a panel to coordinate the plans of the various ministries to bolster the country's exports.
The panel, to be called the Export Promotion Board, will be on the lines of the existing Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) to facilitate exports, the government said in a statement.
The FIPB is India's central authority for approval of foreign investment proposals into the country and is empowered to clear projects of upto six billion rupees each ($168 million).
Gujral, at the end of a marathon five hour session with exporters and industry officials, said the government and business must come together to accelerate exports.
India's exports in April were estimated at $2.52 billion, down from $2.81 billion in the same month last year.
The prime minister agreed to set up a single window clearance system for the export processing zones to improve the efficiency of exports from various zones.
Gujral also announced a number of policy initiatives for the textile sector which accounts for a substantial part of India's total exports.
India exported textiles worth $7.1 billion during April-December 1996, a growth of 11.6 percent over the same period in the previous year.

Gujral said he will discuss the issue of setting up of a cotton technology mission on Saturday to increase productivity of Indian cotton and to give a major thurst to country's cotton and textile exports.
He also directed the Finance Ministry to take up a proposal for immediate setting up of the technology upgradation fund for the textile sector.
